speaker: james_burbage
text: You are in. Shut the door. The gate looked at you once, and it can look again if you leave the door swinging.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: It looked at every face, Master Burbage. From Bishopsgate up, the street is swept, and quieter than a Sunday.

speaker: john_heminges
text: Quieter, and empty of a play at two. The almanac says no play. The afternoon bill was struck this morning, before we had well sat down to know it.

speaker: augustine_phillips
text: Struck, and the wardrobe chests still have Saturday's second iron on them. I should like a morning that does not begin with a lock.

speaker: george_bryan
text: Then this is the morning we kept for ourselves on Saturday. We were to meet, and see what Monday was. Monday is this table.

speaker: richard_burbage
text: And what hast thou brought us, Will, if the yard is dark?

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: The only thing in the room that was mine to bring. Forty leaves. A king. I will read him, if you will sit for him.

speaker: james_burbage
text: Sit, then. I will hear a king at my own table. Hearing is not playing, and I want the City to be able to tell the two apart.

speaker: john_heminges
text: Read him through, Will. If we are to know what we are holding, we had better have heard the page.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Every voice, then. Stop me when you have had enough. I do not think you will.

speaker: george_bryan
text: Begin. The watchmen have had their look. Let the house be about a book.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: For Gods sake let vs sit vpon the ground.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: And tell sad stories of the death of Kings.

speaker: richard_burbage
text: Leave thy hand out of it. No. Leave mine. I am not done with the line.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I am not taking it from thee. The hand stays. The king goes on, Dick.

speaker: augustine_phillips
text: Go on. I can bear a sad story, if nobody fetches a drum for it.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: No drum. He is on the ground. The ground is doing more than we are.

speaker: john_heminges
text: I will hear it out. This hour I am asking what the page says, and not what a bill may carry.

speaker: james_burbage
text: The page may say what it likes in my parlour. A parlour is not a stage. I am particular about which of mine is which.

speaker: george_bryan
text: Read the next, Will. None of us is at the Mayor's door now. We are at a table, and the table can bear it.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Next, then. You have the hollow crown in the room. The harder page can wait until we come to it.

speaker: richard_burbage
text: Come to it. Thou wilt not find the hand shifted when thou lookest.

speaker: augustine_phillips
text: Kemp is not in the house. He will be stopped at a door between the gate and ours, taking the news in both ears.

speaker: john_heminges
text: Let him stop. A book does not wait on a man's news. Read, Will.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I am reading.

speaker: george_bryan
text: And we are not yet at the end of him. Good. I would rather meet the end with the morning still on our side.
